summary: Describes a graphics loader on the Project MAC PDP-10 that lets remote ARPANET users send display programs to the Evans and Sutherland LDS-1 and run them repeatedly. Local users can also use it for ARDS and Imlac consoles.

plainLanguage.summary: The Graphics Loader lets a remote user send a drawing program to a computer with an LDS-1 display and run it there. The service can return the visible drawing data and accept updates to the program.

subtitle: A remote service for running graphics programs on an LDS-1 display.

tldr.problem: Remote ARPANET users wanted graphics output from programs run on the LDS-1 display at the Project MAC computer.
tldr.mechanism: The Graphics Loader accepts a display program, runs it on request, captures visible line coordinates in memory and sends selected data back to the originating site.
tldr.outcome: Users could reuse a loaded program and send changes or parameters rather than retransmitting the whole program each time.

sections.title: Remote Use of the LDS-1
sections.content:
The Graphics Loader on the Project MAC PDP-10 supports the Evans and Sutherland LDS-1 display. Remote users can send display programs to it and receive the resulting output in digital form. Local users can also use the facility for ARDS and Imlac consoles.

The program need not be sent again for every run. Users can send corrections or changes, and provide varying data or parameters separately.
sections.plainLanguage: A remote user can run a graphics program on the LDS-1 and receive its output over the network. After sending the program, the user can send only changes or new parameters.

sections.title: Requests and Execution
sections.content:
Requests use 36-bit words. The first word identifies an operation; some operations also read an argument word. The six operations are SETUP, EXECUTE, TRANSMIT, UPDATE, FLUSH and MODESET.

SETUP loads a program and reserves output space. EXECUTE runs it. TRANSMIT sends program or output data back. UPDATE changes program data, FLUSH ends the connection, and MODESET controls acknowledgements and automatic transmission behavior.
sections.plainLanguage: The user sends commands to load, run, change or retrieve a display program. The user can also set feedback options or end the connection.

sections.title: Capturing Visible Output
sections.content:
The LDS-1 can write the coordinates of visible line-segment endpoints into memory. It uses a Writer Address Register (WAR) to mark the output area. Before each run, the loader sets the display mode and initializes the WAR; afterward, it uses the final register value to determine how much output was produced.

The loader can transmit the stored output as an exact copy or, in a specified mode, convert line coordinates to ARDS format.
sections.plainLanguage: The display writes coordinates for visible lines into a reserved memory area. The loader uses that area to determine what output to return to the user.
